#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Set up a thesis project, or upgrade one, from the thesis-agnostic workflow in workflow/
# (ai/, agents, hooks, research method docs, dev environment). The skills themselves stay user-level.
#
# Usage: setup.sh [dest]                                    new project (dest defaults to the current directory)
#        setup.sh --upgrade [--dry-run] [--take FILE]... [dest]
#
# An upgrade is three-way. ai/workflow-manifest.txt records the skill's version of every workflow
# file the project last took. For each file in workflow/:
#   - only the skill changed it      → replaced
#   - only the project changed it    → kept (the project's own edit)
#   - both changed it                → conflict: kept, listed, replaced only when named with --take
#   - the project does not have it   → added
# It never touches the research itself, ai/project.md, or profiles the project added to ai/profiles/.
# A project set up before the manifest existed has no record: every differing file is a conflict.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="$(dirname "$(realpath "$0")")/workflow"
MANIFEST=ai/workflow-manifest.txt
UPGRADE=0 DRY=0 TAKE=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --upgrade) UPGRADE=1 ;;
    --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
    --take) shift; TAKE+=("$1") ;;
    *) break ;;
  esac
  shift
done
DEST="$(realpath "${1:-$PWD}")"

[ -d "$SRC/ai" ] || { echo "No workflow found at $SRC." >&2; exit 1; }

hash() { sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }
src_files() { (cd "$SRC" && find . -type f -printf '%P\n' | sort); }
write_manifest() {  # the skill's hash of every file, except those passed (unresolved conflicts keep their old entry)
  local skip=" $* " old
  {
    while IFS= read -r rel; do
      if [[ "$skip" == *" $rel "* ]]; then
        old=$(grep -F "  $rel" "$DEST/$MANIFEST.old" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
        [ -n "$old" ] && echo "$old"
      else
        echo "$(hash "$SRC/$rel")  $rel"
      fi
    done < <(src_files)
  } > "$DEST/$MANIFEST"
}

if [ "$UPGRADE" -eq 0 ]; then
  [ ! -e "$DEST/ai" ] || { echo "$DEST already has ai/: already set up, nothing copied. To update its workflow files, use --upgrade." >&2; exit 1; }
  # -n: never overwrite a file the project already has.
  cp -rn "$SRC/." "$DEST/"
  mkdir -p "$DEST/research/0-start" "$DEST/research/ai-log/decisions" "$DEST/research/ai-log/raw" \
           "$DEST/research/sls" "$DEST/research/dsrm"
  write_manifest
  [ -d "$DEST/.git" ] || git -C "$DEST" init -q
  echo "Copied the workflow ($(src_files | wc -l) files) from $SRC to $DEST."
  exit 0
fi

[ -d "$DEST/ai" ] || { echo "$DEST has no ai/: not a thesis project. Run without --upgrade to set it up." >&2; exit 1; }

replace=() keep=() conflict=() add=()
while IFS= read -r rel; do
  dst="$DEST/$rel"
setup.sh
SKILL.md
workflow

# Protocol change: key-papers

Saved as `sls/1-protocol/changes/2026-10-12-key-papers.md`.

- `sls/3-reading/step.md`, *Rules*:
  - Before: "Papers my argument depends on are read in full by me." No test said which papers those are, and the 3c skill asked for them to be read before each 3c decision.
  - After: a paper is key if it passes at least one of four tests (sole or main evidence for an SQ; a claim the problem or gap rests on; strongest counter-evidence; a seed in `0-start/seeds.md`). Key papers are proposed at 3c (provisional), updated at each 4b from the papers each accepted concept rests on, extended at 5c with any paper `5-gap/gap.md` rests on, and read in full by me before the gap gate (5c) is decided.
- Outside the protocol, to match: `ai/flow-sls.md` rows 3c, 4b and 5c; the `sls-3-reading`, `sls-4-synthesis` and `sls-5-gap` skills.

## Why
Which papers I read in full was decided case by case, from the assistant's proposal, with no stated rule. At 3c the argument does not exist yet: it is built at synthesis (4a) and the gap (5a), so which papers it rests on can only be known from the concept files and `gap.md`.

## Papers affected
None re-screened or re-read. P8, P9, P10 and P12 no longer wait at 3c for my full reading; they are read before 5c if they are key.

# FAQ

**How do I pick the start set?**
- Papers that are clearly relevant and come from different communities, publishers, years, and authors, so the snowball does not stay inside one group [1].
- Wohlin suggests Google Scholar to find them, to avoid bias toward one publisher [1].
- Candidates, all to be checked against the protocol: Hewitt [2], Agha [3], Kay [4], Dally [5], Woodruff [6], Backus [7].

**How do I decide whether a candidate is in?**
- Look at title first, then abstract, then the full text if still unsure [1].
- Apply only the criteria in `1-protocol/criteria.md`. If you want a new criterion, log a change in `1-protocol/changes/` first.

**When do I stop?**
- When an iteration finds no new papers [1]. Not when you are tired, and not when the matrix "looks done".

**Why not search databases with keywords instead?**
- Terms in this area are not settled (actor, object, message-driven, capability), so keyword searches miss papers. Snowballing follows the citations the authors themselves made [1].

# FAQ — general

**What methodology is this?**
- Design Science Research: learn by building an artifact and testing it [3].
- The process is the Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM) of Peffers et al. [8].
- The *artifact* is what you create: here, the actor machine's instruction set, language, and simulator.

**Why follow the sequence instead of jumping between steps?**
- The sequence is the paper's contribution: a common, recognizable process for design science work [8].
- It is *nominally* sequential: you may enter at a later activity, and you may iterate back [8]. It is never a free-for-all.

**Which entry point am I using?**
- Problem-centred: the research starts from an observed problem [8]. That is `../0-start/observation.md`.

**Where is the iteration?**
- On Peffers' iteration arcs: from Evaluation or Communication back to Objectives or Design [8].
- Iterating **rewrites filled blanks**, because a later step taught you something. Filling writes into empty ones.
- This is Simon's *generate–test cycle* [4]. Hevner calls design a *search process* [3].
- Git history is the iteration record. If it only adds text and never changes earlier text, you are filling, not iterating.

**Where does the literature fit?**
- It is not a DSRM activity. Activities 1–3 draw on knowledge of the problem, of current solutions, and of theory [8].
- This is Hevner's *rigor cycle*: research draws on the knowledge base and adds to it [2].

**Is this a Minimum Viable Product cycle?**
- It is similar: build the smallest testable thing, learn, repeat [5].
- It is different:
  - it tests a research question, not user demand;
  - it must be grounded in literature [2];
  - it may change the question itself;
  - it produces knowledge, not a product.
- In the thesis, say *prototype* and *build–evaluate cycle*.

**How do I structure the repository?**
- Create a folder only when a real file needs it: "You Aren't Gonna Need It" [6][7].
